Enter your Loxone and Hue adapter instan: Enter your Loxone and Hue adapter instances plus bridge access below. Lamp mapping is on the 'Lamps' tab.
For direct bridge access (scene creation: For direct bridge access (scene creation/recall, which the hue adapter itself cannot do): the bridge IP is taken automatically from the hue adapter's own config if left empty here. The API token must be entered once by hand (it's in the hue adapter instance's own config under 'user', but that field is protected and can't be read automatically from another adapter).
Hue bridge IP (empty = use hue adapter's: IP моста Hue (пусто = использовать из адаптера Hue)
How long a light visibly fades between i: How long a light visibly fades between its old and new brightness/color. In milliseconds - 700 ms is a smooth, unhurried default; 0 = instant/no fade.
When several lights in a room change wit: When several lights in a room change within this time window, they're sent to the Hue Bridge together (in parallel) instead of one after another - this is what makes a scene switch on all at once instead of visibly rippling across the room. Increase if lights still seem to lag behind each other; decrease for a snappier (but more sequential-looking) response.
How often the adapter re-checks all ligh: How often the adapter re-checks all lights that should currently be off and turns off any that have drifted on (e.g. someone used a Hue app or physical switch directly). Set to 0 to disable this safety check entirely.
The adapter learns each room's Loxone \": The adapter learns each room's Loxone "mood" (light scene) and, once learned, recalls it as a single Hue Bridge scene instead of many individual light commands - this avoids lights switching on with a visible stagger. The settings below tune that learning process.
After a mood is activated in Loxone, the: After a mood is activated in Loxone, the adapter waits for this much quiet time (no further value changes) before it considers the mood "settled" and worth caching as a Hue Bridge scene.
Some Loxone moods never settle because t: Some Loxone moods never settle because they constantly change color/brightness on their own (e.g. a "Party" scene). If a mood hasn't settled within this time, the adapter marks it as "dynamic" and stops trying to cache it as a fixed scene - it will instead be applied light-by-light every time.
Below this many lights in a room, the ov: Below this many lights in a room, the overhead of creating/maintaining a dedicated Hue Bridge scene isn't worth it - the adapter just applies each light individually instead.
Color temperature for plain dimmer outpu: Цветовая температура для простого диммера (mired, 0 = никогда)
Applies only to white-ambiance (tunable-: Applies only to white-ambiance (tunable-white, non-color) lights whose Loxone output is a PLAIN dimmer (no color info at all) - in that case Loxone can't express any warmth, so this fixed value is applied ONLY the moment the light turns on from off; later brightness changes never touch it again, so you're free to fine-tune it anytime in the Hue app without the adapter fighting you. Set to 0 to never set it automatically (fully hands-off). If the Loxone output IS color (RGB) but the paired Hue light is white-ambiance-only, the adapter instead automatically derives an approximate color temperature from that RGB color on every change (not configurable, always on) - this fixed value is not used in that case. Mired scale: lower = cooler/bluer, higher = warmer/more orange; typical range 153 (very cool) to 500 (very warm), 454 is a warm candle-like white.
Scales down the MAXIMUM brightness of co: Scales down the MAXIMUM brightness of color (RGB) lights only - has no effect on color/hue accuracy. E.g. 0.4 means Loxone's 100% brightness only ever reaches 40% of the light's true maximum. Lower this if color lights look too intense/harsh next to white lights at full brightness; raise towards 1.0 for full brightness range.
All lamps in one list. For 'Loxone outpu: All lamps in one list. For 'Loxone output', pick the light-controller output BLOCK itself (e.g. "AI2"), not one of its individual sub-values - the adapter automatically figures out and uses the right one (.rgb/.position/.active) based on your Hue lamp's detected type. 'Loxone context' is read-only/informational, kept up to date by the adapter itself (format "group::Loxone name (Type X)") - it's not editable here.
